SOURCE: Written for this benchmark: the products of each of B4's mechanism steps (b4-mechanisms.json and the 12 of scripts/arrow-gallery.mjs), as the step's curved arrows make them, by hand; and two E2 steps on bromocyclohexane chairs (Br axial, every H drawn, hydroxide taking the H on C2 anti-periplanar to Br), in the two chair drawings. Where an arrow from a bond goes to an atom, the end of the bond that bonds to it is the chemist's: HBr addition gives the secondary cation (Markovnikov), hydroboration puts B on the terminal carbon, epoxides are opened at the CH2 by hydroxide and at the CH under acid, as the arrows' targets say. The E2 on a Newman projection gives (E)-but-2-ene: the two methyls are anti (180 degrees apart) in the drawn conformation (worked out from newmanDoc's angles in b6-canonical.mjs and checked there).

chairs.note: hydroxide takes C2's axial H, anti-periplanar to the axial Br on C1
